general_background.title: Aminoarsine conversion depends on reduction
general_background.summary: An aminoarsine provides an alternative arsenic feed in colloidal indium arsenide synthesis. Its transformation depends on the reductant environment, which can change how quickly arsenic becomes available to nucleating and growing nanocrystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Monodisperse InAs Quantum Dots from Aminoarsine Precursors: Understanding the Role of Reducing Agent

general_background.title: An amino-substituted phosphorus precursor must first react
general_background.summary: Tris(diethylamino)phosphine is an amino-substituted phosphorus source rather than a preformed metal phosphide. Its precursor chemistry affects how rapidly phosphorus becomes available to the indium feed and growing crystals.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Aminophosphines: A Double Role in the Synthesis of Colloidal Indium Phosphide Quantum Dots

general_background.title: A primary amine can change surface growth
general_background.summary: Oleylamine can coordinate soluble metal species and bind exposed surface sites during colloidal growth. It can therefore change how rapidly precursors react and how readily the resulting particles remain dispersed.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Nucleation and size focusing
general_background.summary: A rapid change in precursor availability can create a short nucleation period followed by growth on existing particles. Growth can narrow the size distribution while material is supplied, whereas later ripening can consume smaller particles and change that distribution again.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution
